summary: April looks like a clean MER win on the surface — MER rose to 4.65x from 4.50x and total POS hit Rs 93.5L on 8.2% less spend. The underlying mix is the concern: Shopify collapsed from 10.4% to 5.7% of POS, so the highest-margin channel halved while Amazon absorbed the volume. Meta spent Rs 1.53L with zero attributed revenue across all 9 ad sets — almost certainly a Shopify pixel or destination-URL issue masking real performance. The portfolio shape is otherwise healthy (Generic 73.7% of Amazon kw spend), but the biggest May lever is fixing Shopify attribution and reallocating from over-funded branded defense plus zombie campaigns into competition conquest and proven generic SBV reach.

recommendations.title: Shopify share fell from 10.4% to 5.7% of POS — the highest-margin channel just halved
recommendations.whatDataShows: Shopify revenue was Rs 5,32,942 in Apr '26 — 5.7% of total POS Rs 93,48,057. Mar Shopify share was 10.4%; the absolute drop is approximately Rs 4-4.5L of Shopify revenue. Amazon absorbed the volume, hitting 91.5% of POS (Rs 85,58,206).
recommendations.whyItMatters: Per Principle 7, a Shopify sale is ~15% higher margin than Amazon and is the only owned customer relationship. MER improved (4.50x to 4.65x), but it improved on the back of Amazon volume, not channel diversification — that is a paid-treadmill warning even when MER looks healthy. Hitting the 18-month 35-40% organic-revenue goal is mathematically very hard if Shopify keeps trending below 8% of POS.
recommendations.exactAction: Run a 5-day Meyer.in audit this week. (1) Verify Meta and Google pixels (and Conversions API) fire on the /thank-you page. (2) Identify any Amazon-exclusive Apr offer that Shopify did not match — that is the most likely cause and the easiest fix. (3) Pull the top 5 Apr Shopify SKUs and confirm they're in stock and featured on the Meyer.in homepage. Until cause is found, do not reallocate any budget away from Shopify-driving Meta retargeting ad sets.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Shopify % of POS should recover to >=8% in May. If still <7% by May 31, the channel is structurally drifting, not a one-month blip — escalate.
recommendations.estimatedImpact: Est. Rs 4-5L/mo of margin lost vs Mar baseline if not recovered

recommendations.title: Meta spent Rs 1,52,714 with zero attributed revenue across all 9 ad sets — pixel/destination audit blocks every Meta budget call
recommendations.whatDataShows: Every Meta ad set shows Rs 0 attributed revenue: Carousel Prospecting Rs 48,277, Catalogue Prospecting Rs 26,768, Instream Rs 25,417, Catalogue Remarketing Rs 16,569, MOF Video Viewers Rs 14,839, two PC launch ad sets Rs 12,017 + Rs 8,827. Click volumes are real (85K, 121K, 34K) and CTRs on Catalogue/Media Mix are 3.93% and 4.99% — engagement is fine.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Meta cannot track Amazon purchases (Principle 7 measurement note) — only Shopify. Given Shopify did Rs 5,32,942 in Apr and ALL Meta is showing zero, this is either (a) the Shopify pixel/CAPI is not firing for Meta-attributed visits or (b) Meta ads are sending users to amazon.in/meyer rather than meyer.in. Both are silent failures of the most expensive measurement infrastructure and they make every awareness-vs-cut decision blind.
recommendations.exactAction: Have engineering verify the Meta pixel + Conversions API on Meyer.in this week — spot-test by running a Rs 500 retargeting ad to a Shopify-only SKU. In parallel, audit each ad set's destination URL: any Meta ad pointing to amazon.in must be paused immediately and rerouted to meyer.in. Paying for Meta clicks that close on Amazon kills both attribution and the Shopify margin advantage.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Meta should show >=Rs 50,000 attributed revenue in May once pixel is fixed (assumes ~half of click value lands on Meyer.in). If still zero, the issue is destination, not measurement.

recommendations.title: Pause 'SP | Top 10 ASIN | Ads Autopilot | KT' — Rs 45,705 at 1.45x ROAS, the autopilot tool is not learning
recommendations.whatDataShows: Spend Rs 45,705, attributed revenue Rs 66,349, ROAS 1.45x, 1,005,387 impressions, 5,847 clicks at 0.58% CTR — a manual-keyword campaign on supposedly top-performing ASINs.
recommendations.whyItMatters: These are the brand's own top 10 ASINs — already have demand and reviews. A 1.45x ROAS here is not a benchmark miss, it is a tool failure. Per Principle 8, this is not a generic recall-builder where a low ROAS is acceptable; it is named-ASIN keyword targeting that should perform. Same product cluster done right ('SP | cast iron frypan Skillit | KT') hits 5.70x at Rs 55,261 — the gap is the autopilot tool, not the inventory.
recommendations.exactAction: Pause this campaign by Friday. Rebuild it as a manually-managed SP Manual KT campaign with the same 10 ASINs, a Rs 1,500/day budget cap, and bids on only the top 20 search terms from the Apr SP search-term report that converted. Reinvest the Rs 45K saved into 'SP | cast iron frypan Skillit | KT' (5.70x) by raising its daily cap by 50%.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Rebuilt campaign should hit >=3.5x ROAS at the same spend level. If still <2.5x in May, the ASINs themselves have a listing or pricing issue that bid management cannot fix.

recommendations.title: Cap branded keyword spend at Rs 3,00,000/month — 17.7% of total spend on defending Meyer is past defensive ceiling
recommendations.whatDataShows: Branded keyword spend totals Rs 3,55,350 across SP/SB/SBV at 5.82x ROAS. SP Manual Branded alone is Rs 3,10,953 at 4.80x. Branded ACOS is approximately 17.2% (Rs 3,55,350 / Rs 20,68,141). Branded is 20.4% of measurable Amazon keyword spend.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Per Principle 3, branded ROAS overstates incrementality — most 'Meyer kadhai' searchers would have bought anyway (typical incrementality 15-30%). 17.2% ACOS is already inside the <20% target, so the team is not bidding aggressively — they are just running too many branded ad sets. Headroom freed here is the cleanest way to fund Competition (Rec 7) and Generic SBV scale (Rec 8) without blowing the spend envelope.
recommendations.exactAction: Cap total branded spend at Rs 3,00,000/month (down ~Rs 55K from Rs 3,55,350). First action: reduce daily budget on 'SBV | Cast Iron Tawa Collection | Page Visit' (Rs 1,54,370 spend, 2.90x — partly branded targeting) by 30%. Hold all SP Auto Branded and SP Manual Branded high-ROAS campaigns at current cap. Redeploy the Rs 55K freed into SP Auto Competition (currently at 2.58x) per Rec 7.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Branded spend should land at Rs 2,90,000-3,10,000 in May. Branded ACOS may rise slightly to 18-20% (acceptable, still inside target). If branded organic orders (SKU-level orders not ad-attributed) hold flat or grow, the cut was safely incremental.

keyMetrics.label: Branded share of Amazon kw spend

recommendations.title: SD retargeting underperforming — overall 1.98x ROAS, two campaigns below 1.5x
recommendations.whatDataShows: Sponsored Display total: Rs 81,404 spend, Rs 1,61,442 revenue, 1.98x ROAS — below the 3x retargeting benchmark. Worst: 'SD | ANYDAY | OWN PT' Rs 9,408 at 0.76x; 'SD | Tope | Own PT | Comp PT | CT | Remarketing | Reach' Rs 16,324 at 1.42x; 'SD | Range | Own PT & Remarketing | CVR' Rs 2,004 at 0.00x. Best: 'Four_Star_SD_Retargeting' Rs 16,830 at 2.95x.
recommendations.whyItMatters: SD should be the cheapest converter — these are users who already viewed Meyer pages. Multiple SD campaigns under 1.5x means stale audience lists, generic creative, or audience windows too wide. This is leakage, not a brand-building cost — none of it is buying reach we need.
recommendations.exactAction: Pause 'SD | ANYDAY | OWN PT' (0.76x) and 'SD | Range | Own PT & Remarketing | CVR' (Rs 0 revenue) immediately. For 'SD | Tope | …' (1.42x), narrow the audience to 7-day page-viewers and refresh the creative to a 3-second product-in-action video. Scale 'Four_Star_SD_Retargeting' (2.95x) by 50% to Rs 25K. Aim for SD overall ROAS >=2.5x by end of May.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: SD overall ROAS should clear 2.5x in May. Pause + reallocate frees ~Rs 12K of clear waste; Four_Star scale-up should add ~Rs 25K of incremental revenue.

recommendations.title: 'SP | Cookware Set | KT' returned Rs 412 on Rs 4,361 spend (0.09x ROAS) — match type is bringing irrelevant traffic
recommendations.whatDataShows: Spend Rs 4,361, attributed revenue Rs 412, ROAS 0.09x, 205,836 impressions, 602 clicks at 0.29% CTR. 'SP | Pressure Cooker Set | KT' shows the same pattern: Rs 5,504 spend, Rs 0 revenue.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Cookware sets are higher-AOV — when matching is right, CVR should not collapse like this. The pattern (low CTR + near-zero revenue) on cluster terms indicates broad-match catching unrelated 'cookware set under 2000' / 'pressure cooker set 5L' queries that don't match Meyer's premium SKUs. This isn't generic recall building (Principle 4) — it is broad-match leakage.
recommendations.exactAction: Pause both campaigns immediately. Pull the Apr SP search-term report and identify which non-Meyer queries (e.g. 'non-stick cookware set under 2000', 'pigeon pressure cooker set') triggered them. Add those as exact-match negatives across the Cookware Set and Pressure Cooker Set portfolios. Relaunch only after listings are audited for price competitiveness and review count >50.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: When relaunched, target 2.0x ROAS at start. If a relaunch within 60 days still shows <1.5x, the issue is product-market fit on the bundles (price ladder vs Wonderchef sets), not advertising.

recommendations.title: Competition keyword spend at Rs 1,00,961 (5.8% of Amazon kw spend) is undersized for a brand explicitly competing with Wonderchef and Stahl
recommendations.whatDataShows: Competition keyword spend: Rs 1,00,961, attributed revenue Rs 2,36,341, ROAS 2.34x. Best line: SP Auto Competition Rs 30,310 at 2.58x. Underperformer: SBV Manual Competition Rs 20,494 at 2.11x with 47.4% ACOS.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Per Principle 5, competition targeting is conquest — a Wonderchef/Stahl shopper who buys Meyer is near 100% incremental. 5.8% of Amazon kw spend on this is too low for a brand at Meyer's competitive stage. Generic at 73.7% is doing the recall work; competition is the share-stealing layer that converts the recall into stolen purchases.
recommendations.exactAction: Increase competition keyword spend to Rs 1,50,000 in May (from Rs 1,00,961). Scale SP Auto Competition (2.58x) by 50%. Add new SP Manual KT campaigns targeting the 5 highest-volume Wonderchef and Stahl SKU search terms (e.g., 'wonderchef nirlon', 'stahl triply kadai 2.5l') at Rs 800/day caps each. Fund this from the Rs 55K freed in Rec 4 plus Rs 12K freed in Rec 5.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Competition share of Amazon kw spend should rise to 8-9%. ROAS may dip to 2.0-2.2x temporarily as new keyword campaigns ramp — that is acceptable for conquest. Watch competitor brand search velocity in Brand Analytics for downstream spillover.

recommendations.title: 'SBV Manual Generic' delivered 9.1M impressions at 2.14x — the recall engine is working, fund it +25%
recommendations.whatDataShows: SBV Manual Generic: Rs 1,95,822 spend, Rs 4,18,681 revenue, 2.14x ROAS, 9,141,690 impressions, 23,498 clicks at 0.26% CTR. Within this, 'SBV | Cast Iron Tawa Collection | Page Visit' leads at Rs 1,54,370 / 2.90x.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Per Principle 4, generic = brand recall fuel. 9.1M monthly impressions at 2.14x is the trade we want — top-of-funnel reach being partially monetized. With Shopify slipping (Rec 1), Meyer needs MORE of this kind of upper-funnel exposure that builds branded search downstream. This is the closest thing in the portfolio to a working flywheel for the 35-40% organic goal.
recommendations.exactAction: Increase SBV Manual Generic budget by 25% (from Rs 1,95,822 to ~Rs 2,45,000) in May. Concentrate the increase on 'SBV | Cast Iron Tawa Collection' (already 2.90x) — push it to Rs 1,90,000. Verify these SBVs point to the Meyer brand store, not individual PDPs, so each impression builds brand association rather than a single-PDP transaction.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Branded search volume in Brand Analytics should grow >=10% MoM. If branded organic orders rise without branded ad spend rising, the SBV investment is doing exactly the job Principle 4 describes. SBV ROAS may dip slightly to 1.9-2.0x as scale takes incremental impressions — that is acceptable for awareness.

recommendations.title: Meta In-stream prospecting at 0.14% CTR — format is failing, redirect Rs 25K into Catalogue + Media Mix
recommendations.whatDataShows: Meta In-stream Prospecting: Rs 25,417 spend, 4,577,007 impressions, 6,244 clicks, 0.14% CTR. Compare same-month Meta: Catalogue Prospecting CTR 3.93%, Media Mix Prospecting CTR 4.99%, Carousel Prospecting CTR 1.35%.
recommendations.whyItMatters: 0.14% CTR is well below the 1% prospecting floor. This is not an attribution problem — clicks ARE measurable. In-stream (mid-roll/pre-roll on Reels/Audience Network) is failing the format test for Meyer's category. Cookware is visual but In-stream is a low-attention placement. Reallocating to higher-CTR formats keeps awareness funding intact (Principle 6) without paying for a failed slot.
recommendations.exactAction: Pause the In-stream prospecting ad set this week. Move the Rs 25,417 monthly budget into Catalogue Prospecting (3.93% CTR — Rs 15K) and Media Mix Prospecting (4.99% CTR — Rs 10K). Do not cut total Meta prospecting spend — this is a redistribution, not a cut.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Meta blended prospecting CTR should land >=3% in May (currently dragged by In-stream's 0.14%). Watch frequency on the receiving ad sets — if it climbs past 4, refresh creative before adding more budget.

recommendations.title: 100+ zero-spend Amazon campaigns (many '-migrated', 'Campaign with presets', 2022-2023 names) — clean the portfolio before May reviews
recommendations.whatDataShows: The Apr campaign report shows ~120 Amazon campaigns with Rs 0 spend (60+ SP, 30+ SBV mostly '-migrated', 30+ SD dating to 2022-2023). Active campaigns with >Rs 1,000 spend number under 60.
recommendations.whyItMatters: Per Principle 8, the goal isn't fewer campaigns — but zombie campaigns clutter Brand Analytics, dilute portfolio reporting, and pose silent risk (paused campaigns can auto-resume after Amazon platform changes with stale budgets). They also obscure which active campaigns are actually building reach. The team needs a clean portfolio to make confident May reallocation calls (Recs 4, 7, 8).
recommendations.exactAction: This week, archive every Amazon campaign with Rs 0 spend in BOTH Mar and Apr 2026 AND created before Jan 2025. Keep an archive sheet (name, ID, last budget, last positive-spend month) in case any need restoration. Rename anything still labelled 'Campaign with presets - …' or 'AD_READY: Bxxxx' to match the SP|SB|SBV|SD | [Category] | [Targeting] convention. Anything that cannot be assigned a category gets archived.
recommendations.watchNextMonth: Active campaign count should drop to <80. Decision-making time on the May review should fall — that is the actual KPI. Set a recurring 'campaigns with zero spend for 2 consecutive months' archive rule to keep the portfolio clean going forward.

dataQualityFlags: Meta showing Rs 0 attributed revenue across all 9 ad sets on Rs 1,52,714 spend — Meta cannot track Amazon, so this is either a Shopify pixel/CAPI failure or Meta ads pointing to amazon.in (not meyer.in). Verify before any Meta cut decision (covered in Rec 2).

Several Amazon campaigns spent with zero attributed revenue this month: SP | Pressure Cooker Set | KT (Rs 5,504), SP | Steamer | KT (Rs 4,624), SBV | Anzen Video Page Visit (Rs 2,517), SP | Pressure Cooker | CT (Rs 427), SD | Anzen | CT | CVR (Rs 1,555), SD | Range | Own PT & Remarketing | CVR (Rs 2,004), SD | Pressure Cooker | OWN PT | Reach (Rs 1,361), SD | Merlot Own and Comp PT | CVR (Rs 224), SD | Circulon-kettle | Remarketing (Rs 107), AD_READY: B07XMQQHF1 (Rs 1,050), AD_READY: B082NZW436 (Rs 143). Confirm these are real zero-conversion months vs. a tracking lag before pausing.

Amazon ACOS column appears to be miscalculated for most campaigns. Example: 'SP | Cookware Set | KT' shows ACOS 10.6% on a 0.09x ROAS campaign — true ACOS would be ~1059%. Many low-ROAS campaigns show suspiciously low ACOS (0.1%-1.3%). Treat the report's ACOS field as unreliable; recompute as Spend / Revenue before acting.

Many SBV campaigns named with '-migrated' suffix at Rs 0 spend (Cast Iron Kadai, Trivantage, Bakeware, Appam Pan, Cast Iron Casserole). Likely duplicate IDs from a platform migration — confirm with the Amazon Ads team if these are legitimate active records or deletable archive entries.

Flipkart 'PCA Tawa 21 Jan' (SELLER_PCA Retargeting): Rs 2,175 spend, 197,093 impressions, 1,460 clicks, Rs 0 revenue — either a Flipkart pixel gap or the retargeting list is stale (campaign name suggests a Jan 2026 audience). Refresh or pause.

Two Meta 'Media Mix Sales Traffic' ad sets ('New Cookware Offer', 'Cookware Offer') are listed with Rs 0 spend, 0 impressions, 0 clicks. Confirm they are intentionally paused vs. setup errors that never went live.
strategicGap: Three things are not visible in this month's data but are implied by the trends. (1) Google Ads is still pending. With branded search defense unfunded on Google, competitors can bid on 'Meyer cookware' with no defense, leaking the branded organic intent that Meyer's SBVs (Rs 1.95L/mo) are paying to create. Activate at least branded-defense Google Search by end of May — it should run as low-spend insurance, not a growth lever (Principle 3). (2) May 2026 contains the wedding/Akshay Tritiya gifting window (Akshay Tritiya was Apr 29, 2026; wedding peak runs through May), and there is no visible seasonality lift in the April spend pacing — no specific 'gift cookware' creative concept, no Cast Iron Tawa Collection or Anyday SKU 'gift edition' angle being tested across Meta or SBV. May spend should pace 15-20% higher than April with explicit gifting creative. (3) Most importantly: the Shopify slip (10.4% to 5.7%) coupled with no visible CRM/email program in the portfolio means Meyer.in is not yet building a repeat-customer base — every Amazon order is one-and-done. The single highest-leverage missing initiative is a post-purchase capture sequence: warranty registration QR code in every Amazon pack, redirecting to a Meyer.in account creation, then a 6-touch email program (warranty confirm + care guide + cross-sell). This is how the 35-40% organic-revenue goal gets built from owned demand rather than cohort-by-cohort paid acquisition. Without this layer, even a perfect Amazon ads optimization will hit a ceiling on MER.
